chunks: And from him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Qudamah ibn Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever intends to visit the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him) with humility, not arrogance, not showing off, and not for fame, his sins will be purified as a garment is purified in water, leaving no stain upon it. And Allah will record for him, for every step he takes, a pilgrimage (hajj), and for every time he lifts his foot, an expedition (umrah).
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and conditions for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (AS)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the theological significance of Ziyarat al-Ashura as a means of spiritual purification, linking physical devotion to inner sincerity (ikhlas). It establishes a profound metric of reward where every step toward the shrine is equated to a complete Hajj and Umrah, underscoring the shrine's status as a focal point of divine mercy in Shia tradition.
